## Solution

**Answer leak check:** The problem statement contains no leaked answers, solution sketches, or formalization notes. Proceeding.

**Key observation.** For a prime $p \le n$, the quantity $\lfloor \frac{\log n}{\log p} \rfloor$ equals the largest integer $k$ with $p^k \le n$. Therefore

$$
S(n) \;=\; \sum_{\substack{p \le n \\ p \text{ prime}}} \Big\lfloor \frac{\log n}{\log p}\Big\rfloor \;=\; \sum_{\substack{p \le n \\ p \text{ prime}}} \;\sum_{\substack{k \ge 1 \\ p^k \le n}} 1 \;=\; \#\{p^k \le n : p \text{ prime},\; k \ge 1\}.
$$

So $S(n)$ counts all prime powers $p^k \le n$ (with $k \ge 1$, i.e. including primes themselves, counted once per power).

**Reformulation via $\pi$.** Grouping by the exponent $k$,

$$
S(n) \;=\; \sum_{k=1}^{\lfloor \log_2 n \rfloor} \pi\!\big(n^{1/k}\big),
$$

where $\pi(x) = \#\{p \le x\}$ is the prime-counting function (terms with $n^{1/k} < 2$ contribute $0$).

**Estimate of the tail ($k \ge 2$).** For $k \ge 2$ we have $n^{1/k} \le \sqrt n$, so trivially $\pi(n^{1/k}) \le n^{1/k} \le \sqrt n$. The number of nonzero terms is at most $\lfloor \log_2 n \rfloor$, hence

$$
\sum_{k=2}^{\lfloor \log_2 n\rfloor} \pi\!\big(n^{1/k}\big) \;\le\; \sqrt n \cdot \log_2 n \;=\; O\!\big(\sqrt n \log n\big).
$$

**Main term ($k=1$).** By the Prime Number Theorem, $\pi(n) \sim \dfrac{n}{\log n}$.

**Combining.** Since $\sqrt n \log n = o\!\big(\frac{n}{\log n}\big)$, we obtain

$$
S(n) \;=\; \pi(n) + O\!\big(\sqrt n \log n\big) \;=\; \frac{n}{\log n}\big(1 + o(1)\big).
$$

Therefore

$$
\boxed{\displaystyle \frac{S(n)}{n} \;\sim\; \frac{1}{\log n} \;\longrightarrow\; 0 \quad\text{as } n \to \infty.}
$$

The sequence is asymptotic to $\dfrac{1}{\log n}$, and in particular converges to $0$.
